item.title: GBPUSD Technicals: The price extends gains and moves above the 100 day MA in the process
item.description:
GBPUSD breaks above its 100-day moving average as Iran headlines pressure the dollar

The GBPUSD is pushing to new highs for the day as reports of a potential compromise between the US and Iran send oil prices and US yields lower, while putting pressure on the dollar.

According to Al Araby Al Jadeed, Qatar and Pakistan have presented a proposal that includes a secret IAEA visit to Iranian nuclear sites and the release of $6 billion in interest on frozen Iranian funds. The proposal reportedly has US approval and some prior Iranian support, although differences remain and official confirmation is still needed.

The market is responding to the prospect of reduced tensions. December crude oil futures have fallen below $96 after trading above $101 earlier. Meanwhile, the US 10-year yield is down 4.6 basis points to 5.089%, moving further away from last week’s high near 5.36%.

Lower oil prices could ease some inflation concerns, while falling US yields reduce the dollar’s interest-rate support. The GBPUSD has been the biggest mover, with buyers pushing the pair above its 100-day moving average for the first time since September 16. Remember, a higher GBPUSD means a stronger pound relative to the dollar—and a weaker dollar relative to the pound.

The headlines provide the catalyst. The technicals define the next steps.

The break above the 100-day moving average at 1.33875 is a positive development for buyers. Staying above that level would be the best-case scenario for keeping the upside momentum intact.

However, the price is moving into an area where buyers have more work to do:

  • 1.33875: The 100-day moving average and the first support level following the break.

  • 1.34056: The 50% midpoint of the decline from the August 2026 high to last week’s low at 1.3136.

  • 1.34314: The 200-day moving average and the next major topside hurdle.

Today’s high has reached 1.3409, taking the price just above the 50% midpoint. Buyers have cleared that level briefly. Now they need to show they can stay above it and build toward the 200-day moving average.

The midpoint matters because it divides the prior decline in half. Getting above it means buyers have recovered more than half of that move lower. Holding above it would strengthen the recovery story.

Why sellers may lean against this area

Even with the bullish momentum, a rally into major technical levels can attract selling.

Traders who bought earlier at lower levels may take some profit. Sellers may also lean against resistance because the levels give them a reference point for defining and limiting risk. If the price breaks above their chosen resistance level and stays above it, the reason for the trade weakens.

That does not guarantee a reversal. It explains why the rally could slow as the price works through the midpoint and toward the 200-day moving average.

What would weaken the bullish move?

The first test is whether buyers can hold above 1.33875. A move back below the 100-day moving average would take some shine off the breakout and shift attention to 1.3371, Friday’s high and last week’s high.

I would not want to see the price move below that level on a correction. A break above last week’s high followed by a move back below it would suggest buyers are struggling to sustain the breakout. That could lead to some unraveling of today’s bullish momentum.

The buyers have made an important move. Now they need to defend it. Stay above the 100-day moving average, and buyers retain the stronger position. Get above—and stay above—the midpoint and then the 200-day moving average, and the bullish story gains further confirmation.

In the video above I talked about the technicals driving the run in more detail.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Treasury Sec. Bessent says we are on the "other side of the energy shock". The price action needs to confirm that claim.
item.description:
One of the most important lessons I learned early in my trading career was that price action needs to help confirm the fundamental story. A story can sound convincing. But for traders, the question is practical: Is the market moving in a way that supports it?

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said during an appearance on 2WAY TV that we are on the “other side of the energy shock.”

There may be an argument that the worst of the initial spike is behind us. But looking at crude oil prices and the technical levels, I am not ready to declare victory.

December crude oil futures reached $101.37 today. Although the price has since slipped below $100, it remains higher by about 0.78% as I speak. Before the war began on February 28, crude was trading around $67. Near $100, that leaves the price roughly 49% above that starting point.

The initial surge that carried crude to its March high of $119.48 may have passed. The higher price burden associated with the move from $67 to near $100 is still very much in place. Coming off the peak and unwinding the increase are two different milestones.

For traders, that is where the technicals help. They give us specific levels to measure whether sellers are taking control and whether the price action is beginning to support the story.

Right now, those levels continue to favor the buyers:

  • $97.00–$98.48: The price remains above this swing area. It is the first support zone sellers need to break.

  • $96.83: The rising 100-hour moving average provides the next shorter-term reference.

  • $94.46–$94.60: The rising 200-hour moving average at $94.46 sits near the 38.2% retracement of the July-to-September advance at $94.60. That puts two technical tools in the same area, making it an important downside hurdle.

The educational point is that a bearish shift develops in steps. Sellers do not need to break every support level before the shorter-term bias can turn lower. But they do need to start breaking support and keeping the price below it.

A sustained move below $97.00–$98.48 would be the first sign of progress. A break below the 100-hour moving average would strengthen that signal. Getting below—and staying below—the $94.46–$94.60 area would provide stronger evidence that sellers are taking control of the recent advance.

Until then, the price is holding above support. Buyers still have the stronger technical position.

The longer-term picture also needs to be respected. Crude remains above its 100-day moving average at $85.86 and its 200-day moving average at $84.45. Those are deeper benchmarks for judging whether a short-term decline is developing into a broader reversal.

Would breaking those moving averages prove that the economic effects of the energy shock are over? No. But it would provide stronger price confirmation that the market is unwinding the increase.

My job as a trader is to recognize what the market is doing now, define where that view would change, and adjust when the evidence changes.

For now, crude oil’s technical bias remains tilted higher. If sellers begin breaking support and holding those breaks, I will respect that shift. The fundamental story gives us something to consider. The price action gives us something to measure.

In the video, I walk through those technical levels, explain what sellers need to accomplish, and look at what would bring the energy-shock narrative into better alignment with the price action.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: US September pending home sales -7.3% vs -0.5% expected
item.description:
• Prior was +0.3%
  • Index 66.0 vs 71.2 prior
  • Sales -12.6% y/y

This is a record low in pending home sales. Everyone is flagging the AI bubble bursting as the main risk for 2027 but another leg lower in housing could be a real problem for the economy, and I don't expect any help from the Fed.

For background. the US pending home sales report provides an early indication of demand in the existing housing market. Published monthly by the National Association of Realtors, it tracks signed contracts to purchase existing homes, rather than completed transactions.

That distinction is what gives the report its value. A home typically goes under contract one or two months before the sale closes, making pending sales a leading indicator for the existing home sales report. It offers a more timely view of how buyers are responding to mortgage rates, prices and available inventory.

The headline measure is the Pending Home Sales Index, with 100 representing the average level of contract activity in 2001. It is an index of activity, not a count of homes sold or a measure of prices. Markets generally focus on the monthly percentage change, alongside annual comparisons and regional details.

Mortgage rates are a key driver. Lower borrowing costs can improve affordability and bring buyers back into the market, while higher rates can quickly reduce purchasing power. However, cheaper financing alone does not guarantee stronger sales if prices remain stretched or suitable properties are scarce.

For the broader economy, housing transactions support spending on renovations, furniture, appliances and moving services. The report therefore helps investors assess household demand and how financial conditions are filtering through the economy.

The main caveat is that signed contracts are not final sales. Financing problems, inspections or changes in buyers’ circumstances can derail transactions. Weather and regional swings can also distort monthly figures, so a sustained trend carries more weight than a single reading.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: AI’s cheap seats are filling up: open-weight and small models take over the machine workload
item.description:
What worries me about the economics of AI is that as models advance, there will be more and more tasks that can be completed by cheap, open source models. For instance, once AI can reliably complete the tax filings of 98% of people, then you won't need a frontier model to do it. That line of thinking is going to work through a whole series of workloads and Scotia has an interesting report today that's somewhat of a case study on a single healthcare company that's aggressively adopting AI.

The healthcare technology firm Scotion spoke to ($2 billion in revenue, 5,000 employees) is running a two-tier model strategy, and the bottom tier is growing fastest. Machine-driven workloads, now about 70% of token usage, are split 50/50 between closed frontier models and open-weight models like Qwen and Kimi. The exec says that could go to 100% open-weight and he credits the switch with major cost savings while arguing that performance hasn’t suffered.

Some notes:

  • Open-weight models cost about 1/5th of frontier models all-in
  • Small language models cost about 1/100th
  • SLMs trained on internal data can be more accurate than large models on repetitive tasks like classifying PDFs
  • SLM adoption is just beginning

That’s the tax-return problem in real life. Classifying a document or summarizing internal research was a frontier task two years ago. Now it’s solved, and a solved task goes to the lowest-cost producer. Every advance at the top of the stack eventually pushes another set of workloads to the bottom.

The frontier labs aren’t losing business here, at least not yet. Human users still default to Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini, and the exec doesn’t expect closed-model spend to plateau in 2027 because new workflows keep coming.

Notably, the company's cloud spend doubled in 2026 overall, which Scotia says is good for compute providers like MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN because they're largely agnostic to which models are being used. More concerning are the frontier labs, where Scotia sees a "mixed outlook" which I take as a diplomatic way of saying "be cautious".

"Token spend per developer is flat lining," the report says, at around $100-$500 per month.

An Anthropic IPO is expected later this year with valuations now seen in the $1.4-$1.5 trillion range.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: Bitcoin Technicals: Sellers regain control, but the range floor remains the next test
item.description:
Bitcoin buyers had their opportunity yesterday. More specifically, the price broke above its 100- and 200-hour moving averages (currently at $81,686 and $82,082 respectively) and extended to a high of $83,038. However, the momentum faded before reaching the next upside target at $84,178.

The price subsequently rotated lower, spent several hours trading between the two moving averages, and eventually broke below both. Over the last few hours, it has remained below those levels, tilting the short-term technical bias back to the downside.

The moving averages currently come in at:

  • 100-hour moving average: $81,687

  • 200-hour moving average: $82,082

Why do those levels matter? They provide a reference for control and risk. Yesterday’s break above gave buyers an opportunity to build momentum. Their inability to sustain that break—and the subsequent move below both averages—put sellers back in the stronger short-term position.

Stay below those moving averages, and sellers retain that advantage. Move back above them, and the bearish argument starts to weaken.

A bearish bias still needs a break of support

Although the bias has shifted lower, sellers still have work to do.

The key downside obstacle remains the $80,106–$81,183 swing area. That zone has repeatedly attracted buyers and helped stall declines since September 18.

There was a brief break below the area last week, but it quickly reversed and was met with solid buying.

The sellers had their shot. They missed.

That failed break is an important lesson. Trading below support does not automatically produce a sustained move lower. Sellers need follow-through. When the price quickly returns above a broken level, it raises questions about the strength of the selling and gives buyers a reason to lean against support again.

Today’s weaker technical bias gives sellers another opportunity. The question is whether they can turn that opportunity into a break that holds.

What would strengthen the bearish case?

A sustained move below $80,106, followed by a break of the nearby $80,000 psychological level, would strengthen the bearish case.

Below that floor, the next major downside target comes near $76,052. That level represents the 38.2% retracement of the rally from the June 30 low to the September high.

For traders, the broken support area would then become a reference for risk. If sellers are taking greater control, rebounds should struggle to reclaim that area. A quick move back above it would warn that another downside break may be failing.

The break creates the opportunity. The ability to stay below helps confirm it.

Bitcoin remains within the broader consolidation between $80,106 and $87,374. The back-and-forth price action has the feel of a coiled spring as traders wait for the next shove.

However, consolidation does not guarantee an immediate break and run. Traders can anticipate a larger move, but the price action needs to confirm the direction.

For now, trading below the hourly moving averages favors sellers. A sustained break of the range floor would add to that bearish bias.

Conversely, a recovery above $81,687 and then $82,082 would weaken sellers’ control and open the door for another upside probe toward $83,038, followed by $84,178.

Trading is about understanding the bias, the risk, and what would change the technical story. The moving averages define the short-term tilt. The swing area defines the next hurdle. How the price behaves at those levels will help determine whether sellers can finally break and run—or whether they have another shot and miss.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Iran agreed to secret nuclear site visits in shift towards compromise, report says
item.description:
Al Araby Al Jadeed is reporting that Qatar and Pakistan have put a “compromise proposal” in front of Washington and Tehran that meets the demands of both sides. The key detail is that the plan, presented to Iranian officials today by Pakistan’s army chief, reportedly already has American sign-off and some prior Iranian approval.

The reported terms:

  • Release of $6 billion in interest on Iranian funds frozen in Qatari banks
  • A “partial response” to Iran’s demand for the return of frozen funds
  • A secret IAEA visit to Iranian nuclear sites, meeting a US demand
  • A framework to stop a return to escalation and restart negotiations

The same outlet cites a source saying a breakthrough to halt escalation between Washington and Tehran is expected to be announced this week. Mediators are still working to narrow the remaining points of contention.

The market reaction is modest with crude is down about $1 per barrel since the headlines hit a half-hour ago. Naturally, traders are reluctant to trade on any Iran headlines, particularly coming from a questionable source.

Still, the structure is creative. Paying out interest rather than principal lets both sides claim a win. Tehran gets cash, and Washington can say the core funds stay frozen. A quiet IAEA visit is the kind of face-saving inspection that has to happen before anything bigger can, though the immediate leaking of a 'secret' visit isn't going to build trust. If Pakistan’s army chief is personally carrying the paper, it’s being taken seriously at a high level.

For oil, a real de-escalation removes some of the risk premium tied to Hormuz and the region. Watch for official statements from Washington, Tehran or Doha but it's going to be a slow-moving process in any event. Obvsiously WTI above $100 and brent above $110 are reasons for the US to seek a deal ahead of the Nov 3 midterms.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: The Nasdaq remains under pressure amid an ugly mix of higher inflation, growth concerns and widening credit spreads
item.description:
The Nasdaq sold off sharply last week as the negative sentiment from higher than expected US inflation data was compounded by growing concerns about the economic outlook.

Credit spreads continue to widen, credit default swap spreads for AI-linked hyperscalers and data center operators have surged to record highs, and the Federal Reserve is forced to keep a hawkish bias amid higher inflation.

Moreover, oil prices continue to surge amid stalled US-Iran negotiations and the ongoing Saudi-Houthi conflict. To sum up, the bearish pressures continue to mount as the stock market seems to be hanging by a thread.

This week, the most important event will likely be the release of the US Flash PMIs on Friday, barring a surprising breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations of course.

If the data disappoints, growth concerns will likely increase, and we could see another selloff in the Nasdaq. Better than expected data, on the other hand, might lead to a relief rally in the short-term but it wouldn’t change the bigger picture as it would just reinforce the need for rate hikes.

 

NASDAQ TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME

On the daily chart, we can see the Nasdaq (US100 CFD contract) broke below the major trendline and extended the drop into new lows as more sellers piled in to target the 28,742 level. If the price gets there, we can expect the buyers to step in, with a defined risk below the level, to position for a rally into new record highs. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break lower to increase the bearish bets into the 26,971 level next.

NASDAQ TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME

On the 4 hour chart, if we get a pullback to retest the broken trendline again, we can expect the sellers to step in around the 30,000 resistance zone, with a defined risk above it, to keep pushing into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to start positioning for a rally into new all-time highs.

NASDAQ TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 1 HOUR TIMEFRAME

On the 1 hour chart, we have a minor downward trendline defining the bearish momentum on this timeframe. The sellers will likely continue to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will look for a break higher to position for a pullback into the 30,000 resistance. The red lines define average daily range for today.

UPCOMING CATALYSTS

On Thursday we get the latest US Jobless Claims figures, while on Friday we conclude the week with the US Flash PMIs.

 

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: US September housing starts 1.221M vs 1.305M
item.description:
• Prior was 1.305m
  • Building permits 1.400m vs 1.395m 
  • Prior permits 1.275m
  • Permits change m/m vs -2.1% prior

This is another disappointment on the housing front and comes after yesterday's survey of home builders showed sentiment at the worst levels since 2012. High mortgage rates are the big problem in the industry, which is in a deep recession. There is a bit of help today in the rates market with US 30-year yields down 6.4 bps to 5.41%.

For background, the US housing starts report offers an early look at momentum in one of the economy’s most interest rate sensitive sectors. Published monthly by the Census Bureau and the Department of Housing and Urban Development, it tracks construction of new privately owned homes, alongside building permits and housing completions.

A housing start is recorded when excavation begins for a building’s foundation. The headline figure is reported at a seasonally adjusted annual rate, showing what a full year of construction would look like if that month’s adjusted pace continued. It is not the number of homes actually started during the month.

For markets, the distinction between single-family and multifamily construction matters. Apartment projects can produce sharp swings in the headline, while single-family starts generally provide a clearer signal of underlying homebuilding demand. Each apartment counts as a separate housing unit, so a few large developments can significantly influence the total.

Building permits are closely watched because they offer a signal of future construction activity. However, authorization does not guarantee that a project will proceed immediately, particularly when financing costs, labour shortages or weak demand make builders cautious.

Housing punches above its weight economically. Construction supports employment and demand for materials, while completed homes generate spending on furniture, appliances and other household goods. That makes the report useful for assessing growth and the transmission of Federal Reserve policy.

The caveat is volatility. Weather, regional disruptions and sampling uncertainty can distort monthly readings, and initial estimates are revised. Investors therefore weigh the broader trend, permits and revisions before drawing conclusions from any headline.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: Morning Kickstart: Dollar mixed as oil tops $100 and European stocks retreat
item.description:
In the morning video above, I take a look at the three major currency pairs—EURUSD, USDJPY and GBPUSD—from a technical perspective. For each pair, I outline the bias, the risk-defining levels and the targets that would give either the buyers or sellers more control. It is important to have a roadmap technically. I help provide your roadmap. 

The North American session gets underway with the dollar mixed but mostly lower, crude oil above $100, and US and European equities are under pressure. Treasury yields are split, with the 2-year yield edging higher while longer-term yields decline.

That combination deserves attention. Higher oil keeps the inflation discussion alive, but the decline in longer-term yields shows that the bond market is not responding with a uniform move higher in borrowing costs.

Housing is the main focus on the U.S. economic calendar. Building permits and housing starts arrive first, followed by pending home sales. Those reports will give traders another look at how the housing market is handling elevated financing costs.

Dollar mixed, with gains concentrated in the Canadian dollar and Swiss franc

The dollar is lower against six of the seven major currencies, although the euro is effectively unchanged.

From the dollar’s perspective:

  • Against the CAD: down approximately 0.39%, with USDCAD at 1.4055.

  • Against the CHF: down approximately 0.33%, with USDCHF at 0.8238.

  • Against the GBP: down approximately 0.28%, with GBPUSD at 1.3339.

  • Against the NZD: down approximately 0.26%, with NZDUSD at 0.5677.

  • Against the JPY: down approximately 0.21%, with USDJPY at 158.14.

  • Against the AUD: down approximately 0.07%, with AUDUSD at 0.6983.

  • Against the EUR: marginally higher, with EURUSD down approximately 0.01% at 1.1209.

The Canadian dollar is outperforming the greenback as oil advances. The euro is the exception to the broader dollar softness, with EURUSD trading near the lower end of its overnight range.

Currency ranges: EURUSD still has room to roam

Using the displayed session highs and lows and the 22-day average ranges (around a month of trading):

  • EURUSD: 1.1205 to 1.1235 — approximately 30 pips, or 46% of its 65-pip average.

  • USDCAD: 1.4046 to 1.4110 — approximately 64 pips, or 102% of its 63-pip average.

  • AUDUSD: 0.6971 to 0.6998 — approximately 27 pips, or 56% of its 48-pip average.

  • NZDUSD: 0.5662 to 0.5689 — approximately 27 pips.

EURUSD has completed less than half of its average daily range, leaving meaningful room for an extension. AUDUSD and USDJPY also have room to roam.

GBPUSD has already covered most of a normal day’s range, while USDCAD has slightly exceeded its average. That does not prevent either pair from extending farther. The average provides context; the technical levels determine where traders can define and limit risk.

Oil above $100 as Middle East risks persist

Crude oil is higher:

  • WTI futures: $101.01, up $2.47 or 2.51%.

  • The separate USOIL quote: $100.56, up $2.33 or 2.37%.

InvestingLive’s “Crude oil surges further amid Houthis attacks on Saudi energy targets and stalled US-Iran negotiations” reports that stalled negotiations and continued Saudi-Houthi hostilities are keeping the geopolitical risk premium elevated. Reports of a possible diplomatic breakthrough remain unconfirmed.

For traders, that leaves oil sensitive to the next headline. A confirmed agreement could change the supply-risk outlook quickly. Continued attacks or another setback in negotiations would keep those risks in focus.

European data show an uncomfortable mix

The European releases combined stronger producer-price inflation with weaker expectations:

  • German PPI: up 1.9% month over month versus 1.5% expected and 1.1% previously.

  • German ZEW economic sentiment: 28.1 versus 30.2 expected and 34.7 previously.

  • Eurozone ZEW economic sentiment: 18.5 versus 23.6 expected and 25.8 previously.

  • Eurozone current-account surplus: €8.7 billion versus €29.2 billion expected and €27.2 billion previously.

The combination is difficult: price pressures increased while the forward-looking sentiment readings disappointed.

European equities are lower:

  • Germany’s DAX: down 0.75%.

  • France’s CAC 40: down 0.80%.

  • U.K. FTSE 100: down 0.52%.

  • Spain’s IBEX: down 0.62%.

  • Euro Stoxx 50: down 0.54%.

  • Italy’s FTSE MIB: down 0.97%.

China holds rates

China left its loan prime rates unchanged overnight. InvestingLive’s Asia-Pacific market wrap also highlighted a stronger yuan fixing alongside weaker Asian equities.

US stocks are lower led by the Nasdaq 100:

The major US stock indices are trading lower across the board. The snapshot of the major indices implied by futures shows:

  • Dow -38 points
  • S&P -15.25 points
  • Nasdaq 100 -122 points

Treasury yields: Longer maturities lead the decline

  • 2-year: 4.7676%, up approximately 0.7 basis point.

  • 5-year: 4.9219%, down approximately 0.7 basis point.

  • 30-year: 5.4330%, down 4.0 basis points.

The larger declines are at the longer end of the curve. Even with those declines, the 10-year yield remains above 5%, keeping financing costs an important part of the housing-market backdrop.

Gold lower; Bitcoin below $82,000

  • Silver: $57.137, up approximately 0.13%.

  • Bitcoin: $81,381, down $459 or 0.56%.

Gold is lower despite the generally softer dollar and declining longer-term Treasury yields. Bitcoin is also lower, trading below $82,000.

North American calendar

All times are Eastern.

  • 8:15 a.m. — ADP weekly employment update. The prior reading was approximately 24.8K. This measures the average weekly change in private employment over a rolling four-week period.

  • 8:30 a.m. — Building permits: 1.39 million expected versus 1.40 million previously.

  • 8:30 a.m. — Housing starts: 1.30 million expected versus 1.28 million previously. The Census Bureau confirms the release time for the September construction report.

  • 10:00 a.m. — Pending home sales: down 0.6% expected versus a 0.3% increase previously. The National Association of Realtors confirms the release time.

Starts measure construction getting underway. Permits provide a look at the potential construction pipeline. Pending home sales track signed contracts for existing homes. Together, they help show whether housing activity is stabilizing or losing momentum.

EURUSD: Sellers press toward the session low

EURUSD is trading near 1.1209, just above the session low at 1.1205. The euro has failed to participate in the gains seen in most other major currencies against the dollar.

The immediate question is whether sellers can break below 1.1205 and stay below. A sustained break would extend the session range and give sellers more intraday control. A break that quickly reverses would show that sellers had their shot and failed to keep the move going.

The session high at 1.1235 is the upside reference. With the range still relatively narrow, there is room for the next technical break to extend.

[Insert EURUSD chart here.]

USDJPY: Buyers need to defend the session floor

USDJPY is trading near 158.14 after declining from a session high of 158.59. The low is 158.04.

That puts the price closer to the session floor, with 158.00 just below it. Sellers have the stronger intraday hand while the pair remains near those lows. A sustained break below 158.04 and then 158.00 would extend that control.

For buyers, holding the low is the first step. They would then need a recovery through the resistance levels outlined in the video to show that the downside pressure is easing.

[Insert USDJPY chart here.]

GBPUSD: Buyers hold a gain, but the high remains a hurdle

GBPUSD is trading near 1.3339, above its session low at 1.3301 but below the high at 1.3363.

Buyers have the gain on the day. The next question is whether they can build on it. A break above 1.3363—and the ability to stay above—would extend their control.

The pair has already completed about 85% of its average range. Further gains remain possible, but buyers need to show follow-through. A rotation back toward 1.3301 would put the day’s recovery under pressure.

In my book Attacking Currency Trends, I emphasize using the technical tools to define risk. The daily range gives traders perspective. A moving average, swing area or retracement level gives them a place to lean, with risk defined and limited.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

It's been a quiet session in terms of news and data releases. item.title: Beyond Data: Why Context is the Next Frontier in Trading AI
item.description:
Two traders can receive the same market signal and reach different decisions. One may be considering a new position; the other may already have substantial exposure to the same instrument.

This was the central point I explored at iFX EXPO Asia 2026 in Hong Kong. As artificial intelligence (AI) needs to consider a trader's circumstances alongside market data.

From Trading Signals to Contextual Intelligence

Machine-learning models can analyse historical market data to identify patterns that might offer trading opportunities.

A signal based on historical prices does not, by itself, account for a trader’s open positions. If it suggests buying EUR/USD (Euro against the US Dollar), someone already holding a large buy position would need to check whether adding to it fits their risk limits.

Contextual intelligence looks at how three types of information interact when traders make decisions.

• Personal context covers the trader's strategy, capital, trading habits, and risk tolerance.

• Market context includes economic developments, volatility, and liquidity, or how easily an instrument can be traded.

• Trade context concerns the position itself, including its size, intended holding period, and stop-loss and take-profit levels.

If market volatility rises while a trader holds an open position, the range of potential gains and losses may widen. Whether this calls for an adjustment depends on the position's size and direction, the trader's strategy, and their risk limits.

If the trader then adds to the position, their exposure increases. A contextual AI system would need to reassess the position against the trader’s strategy and risk limits, taking higher volatility into account.

Scenario Analysis Before a Market-Moving Event

Consider a trader holding a forex position 30 minutes before a major economic announcement. An AI workflow could examine how the position might be affected by different market reactions, using current market data and information about the trader’s exposure.

The analysis would outline possible outcomes rather than predict how markets will respond to the announcement.

The trader could then assess whether the position still fits their risk limits. Depending on their trading plan, the trader might decide to maintain it open, reduce their exposure, or close it before the announcement.

Different Markets Can Carry the Same Risk

A trader might hold buy positions in gold (XAU/USD), EUR/USD, and the Nasdaq-100, assuming their risk is spread across different markets. Yet all three can be affected by changes in US interest-rate expectations.

On 23 September 2022, gold prices, EUR/USD, and US equity indices all declined amid expectations of further interest-rate increases and growing recession concerns. A trader holding buy positions across these markets could have faced losses on several trades at once.

A contextual AI system could examine these overlapping exposures and assess how simultaneous market movements might affect the account. The trader could then review their total exposure before deciding whether any adjustments are necessary.

AI can Generate a Strategy, That Does Not Validate it

Towards the end of my iFX EXPO discussion, I raised a concern about how traders sometimes use generative AI.

Someone might ask a chatbot to produce a profitable trading strategy and receive detailed trading rules, an explanation of the approach, or even computer code.

A detailed answer can easily be mistaken for a tested one.

Large language models (LLM) can generate inaccurate information and make unsupported assumptions. Without reliable data, a defined methodology, and proper testing, traders have little basis for judging whether the proposed strategy is sound.

I would encourage traders to start with a specific problem in their trading process and use AI to investigate it with reliable data and a clearly defined methodology. The findings can then be checked against actual trading records and market conditions.

For me, the next stage of trading AI moving towards contextual trading intelligence systems that build on existing trading tools. Such systems could support traders as they evaluate opportunities, manage positions, and review their performance, with the analysis adapting as market conditions and individual circumstances change.

Ultimately, the value of trading AI should not be measured by how confidently it generates a signal, but by how effectively it helps traders understand the risks, assumptions and implications behind a potential decision.

AI can broaden the analysis. Context can make it more relevant. Human judgement remains essential.

About the Author

Dr Parker Tian is Head of EBC AI Lab at EBC Financial Group. He presented The Data Isn't Enough: Contextual Intelligence for Trading Decisions at iFX EXPO Asia 2026 in Hong Kong, exploring how AI-assisted analysis can support trading decisions.

EBC Financial Group was recognised as Most Trusted FX Broker and Best CFD Broker at the World Finance Forex Awards 2026. At the UF Awards APAC 2026 awards ceremony held in conjunction with iFX EXPO Asia in Hong Kong, EBC Financial Group was awarded the Best Broker – APAC.

This article was written by IL Contributors at investinglive.com.

USD:

The US dollar has recently come under some pressure as Treasury yields dropped significantly following the higher than expected US inflation data last week.

The reaction might seem illogical as higher inflation should lead to higher interest rates, but the market might be starting to worry about growth.

If economic activity deteriorates, the Fed might be forced to keep a hawkish bias due to persistent inflationary pressures. This could put further pressure on economic growth and eventually require rate cuts.

In fact, further out the curve, we saw a slightly dovish repricing in interest rates expectations despite hot inflation and no changes on the geopolitical side.

If the market’s focus shifted to growth concerns, then the US Flash PMIs on Friday will be a key test. Strong data could quell those fears and give the US dollar a boost. A soft report, on the other hand, will likely increase growth concerns and put further pressure on long-term Treasury yields and the greenback.

 

INR:

On the INR side, the rupee rallied sharply last week after the RBI stepped in to curb its depreciation through a combination of direct FX intervention and regulatory measures. The central bank reportedly sold dollars to support the rupee, while introducing a special facility to supply dollars directly to state-run oil companies, redirecting significant dollar demand away from the spot market.

It also tightened FX derivative rules to make speculative dollar positions more expensive and limit further pressure on the currency. These measures forced traders positioned for further rupee weakness to reassess their exposure, triggering a sharp rebound. However, the intervention does not resolve the underlying pressures from elevated oil prices and foreign capital outflows.

The main driver continues to be oil. India is heavily dependent on imported crude, meaning higher oil prices require Indian importers to buy more dollars to pay for energy, increasing demand for USD and worsening the country's trade and current-account position. The current divergence with oil is therefore unlikely to last much longer and we could see the rupee coming under more pressure in the next days.

In the big picture, the Indian Rupee remains on a bearish structural trend against the US dollar, so dip-buyers will continue to look for opportunities around strong major technical levels to keep pushing the USD/INR pair into new highs.

item.title: Germany October ZEW survey current conditions -35.9 vs -45.0 expected
item.description:
• Germany October ZEW survey current conditions -35.9 vs -45.0 expected
  • Prior -47.1
  • Germany October ZEW survey economic sentiment 28.1 vs 30.0 expected
  • Prior 34.7

The breakdownIt's a mixed showing as the current conditions index shows a marked improvement but the expectations/outlook index falls further in October. The latter is the softest reading since July and marks a turn in optimism towards the German economy in the coming six months.

ZEW notes that while the headline measure might have improved, private consumption and investment are still weak amid higher energy prices. And while the economy as a whole is slowly emerging from stagnation, the recovery itself is still "not self-sustaining".

The readings here will do little to convince of better times up ahead for the euro area economy, not least with French fiscal risks and a more dicey bond market backdrop to deal with currently.

What does the data measure?The ZEW survey measures financial analysts' and institutional investors' views on Germany's economy. The expectations index looks six months ahead, while the current conditions index assesses the present economic situation.

Why does it matter to markets?Germany is Europe's largest economy, so changes in confidence can offer an early indication of where Eurozone growth may be heading. Markets will be watching whether forward-looking optimism holds up or starts to deteriorate.

How does this fit the broader economic picture?Germany's recovery remains fragile, with weak industrial activity, elevated energy costs and subdued domestic demand weighing on growth. Government spending and exports have supported optimism, but the improvement in sentiment has yet to translate convincingly into stronger economic activity.

What is the potential market impact?Stronger readings could offer modest support to the euro and German equities, potentially lifting bund yields on improved growth expectations. Meanwhile, weaker readings would reinforce growth concerns, although any bond market reaction will also depend on inflation and ECB rate expectations - alongside fiscal risks from France based on the latest backdrop.

Current relevance to markets?Modest at best. With French fiscal uncertainty, elevated energy prices and higher bond yields dominating the European market narrative, the ZEW survey is unlikely to be a major catalyst unless the readings deliver a substantial surprise. And even then, the relative impact should be rather minimal.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: BOJ reportedly may upgrade inflation forecast, hold rates steady at next week's meeting
item.description:
The Reuters report is citing four sources familiar with the BOJ's thinking, in saying that policymakers may slightly upgrade their inflation forecast for the fiscal year 2027 as rising oil prices continue to feed through to consumer prices. However, the central bank is still expected to leave interest rates unchanged at 1.25% on 30 October.

That is not all too surprising after the rate hike back in September. And in fact, traders are also pricing in virtually no chance of another rate hike for next week. As for December though? Well, that is a bit of a different story. Traders are assigning roughly 73% odds of another move in the final month of this year.

And that is what markets should be focusing on, rather than being distracted by the immediate outlook next week.

The report also suggests that policymakers are of the view that underlying price pressures haven't changed materially, with little evidence of a broader wage-price spiral taking hold. In other words, it is to say that the BOJ isn't necessarily all too worried about inflation running away just yet.

As such, policymakers are trying to imply that they do have some breathing room to assess the impact of September's rate hike.

Having said that, the central bank may not have the luxury to keep getting away with this sort of move. Higher oil prices, coupled with the risk of further yen weakness, could keep imported inflation elevated for longer. And if those pressures start feeding into broader price expectations, that will spell trouble for the BOJ if they decide to sit on their hands for too long.

But even so, let's be reminded of the fact that raising interest rates will do little to solve Japan's plight. Another rate hike won't help in creating more barrels of oil to address the supply issue. And with regards to the yen, it's a slippery slope with the effectiveness of intervention efforts already proving to be rather questionable as of late.

For now though, markets are agreeing that the BOJ can afford to wait in October. The bigger question is whether the central bank can still afford to wait in December and also for next year, amid pressures of needing to step up the pace of policy tightening.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: German producer prices hit highest since March 2023 as energy costs soar, fueling inflation worries
item.description:
• Germany September PPI +1.9% vs +1.5% m/m expected
  • Prior +1.1%
  • Germany September PPI +6.7% vs +6.2% y/y expected
  • Prior +4.6%

The breakdownWell, this marks another solid jump in German producer prices with the annual rate climbing to 6.7% now in September. That marks the strongest year-on-year increase since March 2023, with rising energy prices continuing to be the main culprit.

Looking at the monthly breakdown, energy prices rose by 5.8% in September compared to the month before. So, much of the headline increase can be attributed to that. If you strip out energy prices, German producer prices were only up 0.1% as a whole in September but still some 3.2% higher relative to the same month last year.

The more detailed breakdown shows more moderate monthly price increases for intermediate goods (+0.2%), capital goods (+0.1%), and consumer goods (+0.2%).

Again, the main worry here is how much of the surge in energy prices will spill over to broader categories. If this keeps up, it feels like it is only a matter of when and not if. And therein lies the worry for consumer prices too, as higher producer prices will eventually trickle down the chain and raise broader inflation pressures in Germany.

In turn, that will keep the ECB in a rather uncomfortable spot amid flagging growth conditions and fiscal worries alongside stubborn inflation.

What does the data measure?The PPI tracks changes in prices charged by German manufacturers for goods sold domestically. It offers an early indication of inflationary pressures before they potentially reach consumers.

Why does it matter to markets?Higher producer prices can squeeze corporate margins or eventually feed into consumer inflation. That makes the data useful for assessing Germany's inflation outlook and the ECB's interest rate decisions.

How does this fit the broader economic picture?The backdrop is increasingly inflationary and growth-negative, with Germany facing rising energy costs alongside consumer price inflation of 3.3%. A further acceleration in PPI would reinforce concerns about stagflationary pressures.

What is the potential market impact?Stronger PPI could reinforce expectations of tighter ECB policy, potentially supporting the euro and pushing European bond yields higher, while weighing on rate-sensitive equities and manufacturers. A softer reading could produce the opposite reaction. But all else being equal, the release here is likely to have minimal impact as a whole as markets place more emphasis on consumer prices.

Current relevance to markets?Moderate. With German inflation accelerating and energy costs remaining elevated, another strong PPI reading would reinforce existing inflation concerns. However, it would  require a substantial surprise or evidence of more persistent underlying price pressures to produce a meaningful repricing of ECB expectations. And that will unlikely be the case just from one PPI report alone here.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: The Floor 8 Moves From Launch Into Its Next Phase of Growth
item.description:
The Floor 8 is entering a new phase of development, building on its launch with an ambition to make trading programs more accessible to eligible traders worldwide.

This next chapter brings together two priorities: accelerating the brand’s growth and strengthening the operational foundations that support the trader experience.

At the center of that strategy is the firm’s 50/50 Evaluation, a model designed to reduce the upfront financial commitment required to begin an evaluation.

A More Accessible Starting Point

The 50/50 Evaluation divides the program fee into two payments. Traders pay half upfront, with the remaining half payable only after successfully completing the evaluation and choosing to activate their funded account.

For traders who do not pass, the second payment is never due.

The approach reflects a straightforward philosophy: giving traders an opportunity to demonstrate their ability before committing the full evaluation fee.

By changing when the fee is paid, The Floor 8 aims to create a more accessible starting point for traders seeking a clearly defined path into its simulated funded programs.

Flexibility Within a Clear Framework

The payment structure is supported by evaluation conditions designed to give traders flexibility in how they approach their objectives.

The 50/50 Evaluation features no daily drawdown rule, no floating-loss rule and no minimum trading days during evaluation. Traders may pass in a single trade if they reach the profit target and meet all applicable requirements.

For eligible traders who prefer to skip the evaluation stage, The Floor 8 also offers an Instant Funded program, providing another entry option into its simulated trading environment.

 

 

Building the Operation Behind the Brand

As The Floor 8 moves beyond launch, its focus extends to the infrastructure and people supporting its programs.

Trading technology, customer support, risk oversight and back-office coordination form the foundation of that work. The objective is to deliver a consistent experience across registration, account access, trading and ongoing support.

The firm’s growth ambitions are tied to developing those capabilities, incorporating trader feedback and refining the experience as its international reach expands.

The Vision of a Modern Trading Floor

The Floor 8 draws its inspiration from the trading floor, a place where ambition, skill and discipline come together.

Its vision is to bring that spirit to an online environment, creating a brand that traders can grow alongside through accessible entry options, clearly communicated conditions and professional support.

The 50/50 Evaluation puts that philosophy into practice: a smaller initial commitment, with the remaining payment linked to successful completion.

Following its launch, The Floor 8’s next phase is about turning that vision into a lasting business and earning trader confidence through the experience it delivers.

About The Floor 8

The Floor 8 is a proprietary trading evaluation firm offering 50/50 Evaluation and Instant Funded programs to eligible traders internationally. Built around the vision of a modern trading floor, the firm aims to make opportunity more accessible while supporting a community shaped by skill, discipline and progress.

item.title: Macro pulse: France's debt crisis doesn't have to get worse to keep hurting the euro
item.description:
France has been the talk of the town in Europe over the past few weeks, and even more so after the weekend riots that we have just seen. Perhaps the only good news is that we haven't quite seen France's debt troubles spiral into a full-blown crisis. But even if things stay exactly as they are, I would argue that France's problems are still a big risk for the euro.

The French-German 10-year yield spread has widened again to around 147 bps as of yesterday, as investors continue to demand a much higher premium to hold French government debt. Now, that is still just below the key 150 bps threshold from the highs earlier this month. So, it's not to say that the latest developments are leading to another euro area debt crisis just yet.

Having said that, I wouldn't label the yield spread at the current level as being reassuring either.

France's borrowing costs are already on the verge of hitting 5%, while Germany's are closer to 3.5%. And with France struggling to get its budget deficit under control, there's little reason for investors to suddenly stop demanding that extra premium. And that is where the euro might be facing a problem.

Even if France's fiscal troubles don't escalate into a wider euro area debt crisis, persistently elevated borrowing costs can still do plenty of damage.

If things keep up, it means that France will have to spend more on servicing its debt as existing bonds mature and are refinanced. And that is money that could otherwise support investment and economic growth. For some context, the European Commission is forecasting the French economy to grow by just 0.8% this year. So, that suggests there is hardly much room to manoeuvre.

Besides that, there is also the risk that investors start demanding a higher premium elsewhere in the region. That might especially be the case in heavily indebted countries like Italy (cue the flashbacks). Now, that doesn't necessarily mean contagion is underway, but it makes the euro area as a whole a much less attractive investment proposition.

Then, there is also the fact that the ECB is facing up against a rather tough balancing act. Higher inflation is leading to higher borrowing costs and that threatens the growth outlook. But for argument's sake, let's just assume the ECB doesn't have an inflation mandate to take care of. Even so, cutting interest rates won't necessarily resolve the fiscal concerns that are driving French yields higher.

So, therein lies the problem for the euro even if there isn't exactly another sovereign debt crisis just around the horizon.

If investors continue questioning France's fiscal outlook while the rest of Europe struggles with sluggish growth, the single currency could remain under pressure even without another major selloff in French bonds. In that lieu, it is important to remember that the absence of a crisis is not the same thing as a healthy market.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: FX option expiries for 20 October 10am New York cut
item.description:
There is arguably just one key expiry level to take note of on the day, as highlighted in bold below.

That being for EUR/USD at the 1.1265 level, with the strike sitting roughly 35 pips away from the spot price. Should the euro manage to build on the hold above 1.1200, the size of the expiries is significant enough to potentially act as a price magnet. Having said that, the euro might find it tough to gather lasting bids as the broader sentiment is still weighed down by French political and fiscal concerns. The expiries on their own may not be enough to draw price higher in this instance.

Besides, there is also the dollar side of the equation to consider. The bond market remains in focus and Treasury yields have nudged back a little higher to start the week. 10-year yields are at around 5.12% today, up from around 5.09% in the early stages yesterday. That may not be indicative of much but if the bond market selloff begins to rear its ugly head again, that could quickly spill over to safety flows favouring the dollar.

If so, that will also push EUR/USD further away from the expiries to be relevant.

Besides that, there is also a decent-sized one for USD/JPY at the 159.00 level. However, it is more than 70 pips away and that arguably sits outside the immediate range of influence for now.
